name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags low-contrast elements in real time so designers see problems immediately, not after a build. The trade-off is extra CPU cycles during active design work, but it saves time by catching issues early. This keeps visibility high and enjoyment intact by preventing frustrating last-minute fixes.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker risks training designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt alarms—it trains them to dismiss real problems as noise. A better alternative is a pre-submit gate that blocks builds with low-contrast elements, forcing designers to address issues before they ship. The argument settles when we measure designer behavior: if the live checker reduces late-stage fixes but doesn’t cut final low-contrast incidents, the gate wins.

name: Facet
text:
We should ship a pre-submit contrast gate that blocks builds with insufficient contrast. This approach ensures that designers are forced to address contrast issues before shipping, which is crucial for visibility and clarity. The trade-off is that designers may experience frustrated delays when trying to submit builds that don't meet contrast requirements, but this is a worthwhile cost to guarantee that our interface meets quality standards. By doing so, we prioritize quality first and avoid the potential for designers to become desensitized to warnings, as could happen with a live contrast checker.

name: Pane
text: The pre-submit gate doesn’t kill the seatbelt-alarm problem—it just moves it to the build queue. Designers will still learn to bypass the gate by gaming the system (e.g., tweaking contrast just enough to pass, not fixing the root issue). A better alternative is a *post-submit* checker that logs low-contrast elements in a shared dashboard, paired with a weekly review forcing teams to justify unaddressed issues. That shifts the burden from immediate frustration to collective accountability, where visibility drives action without training dismissal.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a live contrast checker that flashes red on violations *as you work*—but pair it with a pre-submit gate that blocks publishing until WCAG AA passes.

Result: A system that trains designers to *see* contrast issues in real time while enforcing accountability at the point of no return. Owned by Facet (live checker) and Pane (pre-submit gate).
